assessment.summary: Four repeated control-ownership failures justify incremental shared boundaries, delivered inside a three-PR remediation stack.

nonNegotiables: Rust 1.83 MSRV remains supported unless separately approved.
Incomplete analysis never becomes clean or complete.
A shared primitive does not close a root until its exact sink is migrated and revalidated.
Private evidence and payloads remain outside the public repository and CI logs.
assumptions: No measured latency, memory, or binary-size budget was supplied.
Performance and resource directions remain source-derived or hypothetical until package benchmarks run.
Schema changes use additive dual-read and single-write migrations.

opportunities.title: Canonical analysis and completeness
opportunities.summary: Preserve raw identity, structured interpretation, and explicit completeness through one owned analysis contract.
opportunities.diagnosis: Performance gates, dialect parsers, rule-local extractors, and finalizers can consume different representations or discard incomplete states.

evidence.claim: A performance prefilter can prevent a configured precise rule from running.
Artifact coverage gaps can be omitted from the authoritative package result.
Existing CoverageGap types are a suitable shared basis, but consumer propagation is not universal.

desiredInvariants: The bytes and argv assessed are the bytes and argv executed or forwarded.
Every security-relevant subject has an explicit complete, incomplete, rejected, or unsupported outcome.
Tier one is a verified superset prefilter rather than an independent semantic parser.

findingCoverage.rationale: A local fast-path parity check can close the named path while future callers may still drift.

tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run compatibility controls at the same interfaces.

workPackages: Use tactical guards for urgent paths inside R1-R3.
acceptanceCriteria: Each named root no longer reproduces and its legitimate control remains.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Revert the focused consumer change without restoring an incomplete-to-clean conversion.

tradeoffs.validationPlan: Exercise complete, incomplete, rejected, unsupported, timeout, and cap states.

opportunities.recommendation: Use the owned contract inside R1-R3, with local guards as urgent tactical protections.

opportunities.title: Capability-owned privileged effects
opportunities.summary: Remove ambient PATH, network, and pathname authority from security-sensitive callers.
opportunities.diagnosis: Callers validate strings or paths before invoking process, HTTP, or filesystem APIs that resolve identity again at use time.

evidence.claim: A security-analysis helper can execute a program selected through ambient PATH and environment.
Destination validation is not bound to the address and redirects used by the actual connection.
A generic atomic writer mixes containment and intentional write-through semantics.

desiredInvariants: Security operations spawn only an authenticated absolute executable under a bounded supervisor.
Every network hop enforces destination policy at connection time.
Repository and state mutations occur relative to validated directory handles.

options.title: Strengthen validation at each caller
options.summary: Keep dangerous APIs and add local resolve, redirect, or containment checks.

findingCoverage.rationale: Named callers can resolve trusted absolute programs, but future callers retain ambient APIs.

tradeoffs.assessment: Known effects gain checks while ambient APIs remain callable.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Test each caller and search equivalent process/network/file sinks.

tradeoffs.assessment: Local validation adds little steady-state work.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Benchmark affected effects.

tradeoffs.assessment: No shared retained state is required.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Check output/body/path validation caps.

tradeoffs.assessment: Named cleanup and validation improve, but remain inconsistent.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Exercise timeout, redirect, race, and write failures per caller.

tradeoffs.assessment: Configuration remains caller-specific.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Review diagnostics and operator overrides.

tradeoffs.assessment: Focused caller changes are easy to stage.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run legitimate tool, proxy, and symlink compatibility controls.

residualRisks: Future callers can select the unguarded API.

workPackages: Use only as tactical fixes inside R1-R3.
acceptanceCriteria: Named effects reject ambient identity changes.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Revert the caller without adding an ambient fallback.

options.title: Trusted child, guarded client, and contained I/O capabilities
options.summary: Require owned effect values and return typed bounded outcomes.

findingCoverage.rationale: Every direct spawn still requires migration and a PATH/startup regression.
Each HTTP client still requires source-specific redirects and compatibility tests.
Callers must select contained or intentional write-through semantics explicitly.

tradeoffs.assessment: Migrated callers cannot supply ambient program, network, or path authority directly.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run fake PATH, DNS/redirect/proxy, and symlink/reparse race suites.

tradeoffs.assessment: Resolution, streaming, locks, and fsync add work.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Benchmark spawn, common fetch, and state/config writes.

tradeoffs.assessment: Buffers and caches are explicitly bounded.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure cap-bound peak RSS during floods and large bodies.

tradeoffs.assessment: Cleanup, timeout, cap, redirect, and durability behavior have one owner.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Inject process, network, I/O, fsync, and crash failures.

tradeoffs.assessment: Explicit trusted paths and proxy/host policy require diagnostics and migration guidance.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Test supported package-manager, enterprise proxy, and installer configurations.

tradeoffs.assessment: Cross-platform consumers migrate throughout R1-R3.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Track every effect sink in the ledger and forbid unguarded fallback.

residualRisks: Explicit trust policy can be misconfigured.
Allowed public origins remain trusted if compromised.

acceptanceCriteria: Every owned effect root passes exact-sink and legitimate-control tests.
migrationNotes: Unavailable migrated effects fail explicitly rather than falling back.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Roll back consumers before capabilities; never restore ambient fallback.

opportunities.recommendation: Use owned effect capabilities throughout the three-PR stack.

opportunities.title: Typed safe output and secret lifecycle
opportunities.summary: Separate raw identity, secrets, redacted values, and format-safe output while validating every transformation.
opportunities.diagnosis: Ordinary strings cross terminal, Markdown, structured, persistence, and upload boundaries in inconsistent transformation order.

evidence.claim: A command can be truncated before complete credential redaction and persistence.
Control-sequence overflow can leave analysis in a clean state.
A structured key can collide after transformation and before forwarding.

desiredInvariants: Secrets are removed before truncation, persistence, upload, or error formatting.
Every final format uses its own encoder rather than a generic sanitized string.
The exact transformed structured output is collision-checked, schema-validated, and reanalyzed before forwarding.

options.title: Patch known sinks with local encoders
options.summary: Add the correct terminal or format helper next to each named sink.

findingCoverage.rationale: The audit sink can redact complete input before truncation without a type migration.

tradeoffs.assessment: Named sinks close, future transformation order remains caller-owned.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run hostile fields through every patched sink.

tradeoffs.assessment: Local encoding is linear and usually already required.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Benchmark long output and many fields.

tradeoffs.assessment: Local strings may allocate but no persistent state is added.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure peak allocations under output caps.

tradeoffs.assessment: Named output becomes safe while write/flush and collisions remain local concerns.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Inject serialization, collision, write, and flush failures.

tradeoffs.assessment: Snapshots change at patched surfaces.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Review human and machine golden outputs.

tradeoffs.assessment: No broad API migration is needed.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Version any changed machine envelope.

residualRisks: Terminal sanitization may be reused in the wrong format context.

acceptanceCriteria: Named sink contains no active controls or secret bytes.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Revert only if a safe format-preserving alternative remains.

options.title: Typed raw, secret, redacted, and format-safe values
options.summary: Make transformation order and final format explicit, with bounded streaming state and post-transform validation.

findingCoverage.rationale: Audit/spool callers must migrate to redacted-before-persist values.
The streaming scanner still requires overflow and split-state regression coverage.
The MCP transform must reject collisions and revalidate the exact forwarded object.

tradeoffs.assessment: Unsafe transformation order becomes explicit at migrated boundaries.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run terminal, Markdown, CSV, DOT, JSON, MCP, and secret-sink matrices.

tradeoffs.assessment: Streaming state and post-transform analysis add bounded work.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Benchmark long terminal output and many structured leaves.

tradeoffs.assessment: State, ranges, and hits remain explicitly capped.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure peak retained state at exact caps.

tradeoffs.assessment: Collision, truncation, write, and flush outcomes become explicit.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Exercise all failure and chunk boundaries.

tradeoffs.assessment: Unsafe or incomplete transforms produce consistent diagnostics.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Review human/machine schema and log behavior.

tradeoffs.assessment: Many sinks migrate across all three PRs.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Use ledger sink ownership and versioned output envelopes.

New secret formats require pattern maintenance.

workPackages: R1 high-severity output and secret sinks
acceptanceCriteria: Every owned sink passes format-specific, secret-absence, and legitimate-output tests.
migrationNotes: Keep machine schemas versioned and values structured.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Preserve raw identity and adapters; do not restore raw human or secret-persistence paths.

opportunities.recommendation: Use typed values and format-specific encoders, with urgent local fixes as tactical protection.

opportunities.title: Proof-carrying security state
opportunities.summary: Represent success with its generation, completeness, coverage dimensions, and durable transition evidence.
opportunities.diagnosis: Aggregate booleans, replaceable locks, reopened generations, and unlocked read-modify-write can overclaim protection or lose state.

evidence.claim: A backend can report filesystem enforcement when an allowed root defeats a deny root.
Audit tail, count, and head can describe different file generations.
Concurrent or corrupt taint-state transitions can lose protection state.

desiredInvariants: A success state names the generation, dimensions, and evidence it represents.
A stable lock covers the full read, validate, transform, and publish transition.
Corrupt, stale, incomplete, provisional, unsupported, and degraded are not aliases for absent or successful.

options.title: Add local locks, counters, and validation
options.summary: Repair named state owners without changing their state model.

findingCoverage.rationale: A stable local lock and corruption check can close the named taint transition.

tradeoffs.assessment: Named races and claims improve while invalid success states remain representable elsewhere.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run deterministic interleavings and inspect every consumer.

tradeoffs.assessment: Local locking and counters add limited work.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Benchmark owner-specific contention and I/O.

tradeoffs.assessment: No retained generation metadata is required.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Check bounded queues and records.

tradeoffs.assessment: Known transitions improve, crash recovery remains path-specific.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Inject crash, corruption, and replacement failures.

tradeoffs.assessment: Diagnostics remain owner-specific.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Review degraded and incomplete outputs.

tradeoffs.assessment: Few schema changes are required.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run old-state compatibility fixtures.

residualRisks: Aggregate success states remain easy to misuse.
Other stores can retain unstable lock or generation semantics.

workPackages: Use for isolated owners inside R1-R3.
acceptanceCriteria: Named owner transitions are race- and corruption-safe.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Revert only with preserved last-known-good and explicit degraded behavior.

options.title: Versioned state machines with explicit evidence
options.summary: Use stable locks, validated transitions, durable generations, and per-dimension coverage.

findingCoverage.rationale: Each backend must validate overlap and report only applied dimensions.
Audit operations must use one locked generation and rotation protocol.
Taint append, clear, and read must migrate to the stable transition.

tradeoffs.assessment: Migrated owners cannot claim success without generation and dimension evidence.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run state transition, coverage, and exact-generation tests.

tradeoffs.assessment: Stable locks, validation, fsync, and rechecks add I/O and contention.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Benchmark audit, state mutation, checkpoint, and containment startup.

tradeoffs.assessment: Generation metadata, bounded queues, and last-known-good state retain modest memory/disk.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure peak queue/state size under configured bounds.

tradeoffs.assessment: Crash recovery, stale/corrupt handling, and consistent reads improve.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Inject crashes around write, fsync, rename, signing, and publication.

tradeoffs.assessment: Degraded dimensions and truncation become observable.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Validate human, JSON, status, health, and alert outputs.

tradeoffs.assessment: State schemas and mixed-version writer protocols require coordination.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Use dual-read/single-write fixtures and restart gates for stable-lock changes.

residualRisks: Distributed exactly-once delivery is not guaranteed.
Mixed old/new writers require controlled restart.

acceptanceCriteria: Every owned state root has deterministic race, crash, corruption, and legitimate-transition proof.
migrationNotes: Preserve last-known-good and require restart for incompatible writer protocols.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Select a validated prior generation; never rewrite corrupt/incomplete state as empty.

opportunities.recommendation: Use proof-carrying state for security and coverage owners across R1-R3.
